bank.title: PART 1: KEY CRITERIA REPORTED

subs.title: How it's reported
items: Dedicated Vascular / Mesenteric / Bowel Section: Often highlighted prominently at the top of the findings.

subs.title: Key Criteria Reported
items: The "Whirlpool Sign": The pathognomonic twisting of the superior mesenteric vein (SMV) and mesentery around the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) counterclockwise.
Vascular Relationships: Inversion of normal anatomy (the SMV lying to the left of the SMA instead of the right).
Bowel Viability: Secondary signs including proximal bowel dilation, bowel wall thickening, or absent Doppler flow within ischemic bowel loops.

subs.title: Sample Finding Block
items: Mesenteric Vessels & Bowel (Volvulus Evaluation): Color and power Doppler interrogation of the upper abdomen demonstrates abnormal spatial orientation of the superior mesenteric vessels, with the superior mesenteric vein and mesentery wrapping in a tight spiral clockwise / counterclockwise around the superior mesenteric artery, producing a classic "whirlpool sign." Visualized small bowel loops appear fluid-filled and mildly dilated. [Add Doppler viability notes: Preserved / Diminished flow within twisted mesenteric structures].

Volvulus is a surgical emergency evaluated using color and power Doppler ultrasound to assess the superior mesenteric vessels, which is critical in neonates and infants presenting with bilious vomiting.

bank.title: PART 2: MODULAR DIAGNOSTIC PHRASE BANK — MIDGUT VOLVULUS / MALROTATION

subs.title: Normal SMA / SMV Relationship (No Volvulus)
items: Transverse color Doppler evaluation of the upper abdomen demonstrates normal anatomical orientation of the mesenteric root, with the superior mesenteric vein (SMV) lying normally to the right of the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) and the third part of the duodenum (D3) passing normally between the SMA and aorta. No "whirlpool sign" is present.

subs.title: Positive Midgut Volvulus ("Whirlpool Sign")
items: Color and power Doppler interrogation of the epigastrium demonstrates a classic "whirlpool sign," characterized by clockwise wrapping of the superior mesenteric vein (SMV) and echogenic mesentery around the central superior mesenteric artery (SMA), diagnostic of midgut volvulus.

subs.title: Isolated SMV/SMA Inversion (Malrotation Risk Without Active Volvulus)
items: Inversion of the normal superior mesenteric vascular relationship is noted, with the superior mesenteric vein (SMV) positioned directly anterior [or: to the left] of the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). Although no active "whirlpool sign" or twisted mesenteric pedicle is seen at this time, this vascular inversion is strongly associated with intestinal malrotation; an urgent upper GI series is recommended for further evaluation.

subs.title: Bowel Ischemia / Viability Concern
items: Ischemia Alert: Invaginated/twisted small bowel loops within and adjacent to the mesenteric whirlpool demonstrate circumferential wall thickening (greater than 3 mm), loss of normal gut signature, and markedly diminished/absent intramural color Doppler flow, concerning for bowel ischemia/strangulation.

subs.title: Proximal Duodenal Obstruction ("Double Bubble" / Truncated D3)
items: Marked fluid distension of the stomach and proximal duodenum (first and second portions) with abrupt tapering and non-visualization of the third portion of the duodenum crossing the midline behind the SMA, consistent with high-grade proximal mechanical obstruction secondary to midgut volvulus or Ladd bands.
